core.big_idea: Christians reason from explicit teaching, apostolic practice, and inference, but must not disguise interpretation as quotation.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate literary and canonical context; do not claim more than the selected text supports.

core.metanarrative_position: Apostolic churches within Church, Scripture, and Christian Hope

claims.statement: The selected passage supplies the principal textual evidence for Command, Example, and Inference.
Christians reason from explicit teaching, apostolic practice, and inference, but must not disguise interpretation as quotation.
The curriculum uses command, approved example, and necessary inference as one disciplined way to reason from the New Testament pattern.
claims.interpretive_hinge: No single verse names this three-part method; the framework synthesizes how explicit teaching, apostolic practice, and warranted inference function across texts.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present this framework conclusion as an explicit biblical command or quotation.

core.interpretation_skill: Identify author/audience/genre; observe context; distinguish explicit statement from inference

learning.foundation_objective: Explain from the passage that christians reason from explicit teaching, apostolic practice, and inference, but must not disguise interpretation as quotation and locate the lesson on the whole-Bible timeline.
learning.extension_objective: Identify the immediate context and genre, then distinguish what the text directly states from a reasonable inference and application.
know: The principal passage is Acts 20:7; 1 Corinthians 16:1-2.
Christians reason from explicit teaching, apostolic practice, and inference, but must not disguise interpretation as quotation.
This lesson sits in Apostolic churches within Church, Scripture, and Christian Hope.
understand: Direct observation must remain distinct from synthesis, inference, framework position, and application.
practise: Retell or analyse the passage using evidence from the text.
Name one faithful response without claiming more than the passage supports.
become: A learner who responds to Scripture with trust, wisdom, worship, service, repentance, or love as appropriate.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.
Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.

family.title: Family Bible Time: Baptism and Union with Christ
family.parent_intro: This week we are revisiting Command, Example, and Inference. Keep the discussion anchored in Acts 20:7; 1 Corinthians 16:1-2 and the big idea: Christians reason from explicit teaching, apostolic practice, and inference, but must not disguise interpretation as quotation.

flow.instructions: Recall where Baptism and Union with Christ fits in the Bible story.
Read selected portions of Acts 20:7; 1 Corinthians 16:1-2.
Ask what the passage directly says and what meaning follows from it.
Use the Baptism and Union with Christ Evidence Grid orally or on paper.
Choose one voluntary response and pray together.
